comment: The terrain MCP surface a generated project gets once it installs @threenative/terrain. `tools` is set-equal to the tool table version 0.1.10 serves. Regenerate with `pnpm tsx scripts/capture-terrain-mcp-tools.ts`.

biome.description: A starter biome's name or alias word (forest, woods, beach, ...), or an inline IBiomeSpec object; a spec cooks with `kit`'s surface and assets, forest's when kit is absent. A species named `arbor:<preset>[@seed]` (for example arbor:oak@7) is a procedural Arbor tree the cook bakes and scatters; needs npm i -D @threenative/procedural-vegetation; set the row's far.impostor beyond 190 m, past the tree's last LOD. Presets: oak, beech, birch, spruce, scotspine, blackspruce, aspen, douglasfir, redcedar, bigleafmaple, cypress, olive, stonepine, acacia, baobab, coconut, banana, kapok, sakura, jmaple, ginkgo, bamboo, saguaro, joshua, fanpalm, araucaria, ipe, jacaranda.

request.description: What the world should be, in any words: a biome, a landform (mountains, hills, canyon, volcano, fjord, ...), water (river, lake, sea, ...) and a size (huge, small); an explicit argument wins over a word. A request with no biome word takes the biome its sea or shape suits, else the forest; `decided` names the word behind each choice and `unused` the words that named nothing. A tree word (oak, birch, aspen, cedar, maple, cypress, olive, acacia, baobab, palm, bamboo, cactus, ...) cooks that Arbor species in place of the kit's tree and is reported as `decided.tree`; a spec's own species rows win, and in a region request the word moves that species to the first canopy row and the community stays. A region word (european, boreal, mediterranean, pacific northwest) cooks that region's own world: the row's real survey as the ground, its plant community as the canopy (several species, each baked at more than one seed), and the starter's own surface, understorey and water, reported as `decided.region`. `kit`, `biome` and `ground` still win over it. A real place's name is not geocoded: pass its latitude and longitude as `ground: { location }` to cook that place's survey.

water.description: IBiomeWaterBody rows that replace the biome's declared water: river (width), lake (radius), ocean (level).

ground.description: Where the ground comes from. "procedural" keeps the landform preset's own noise; { heightmap } names a 16-bit grayscale PNG or a square .r16 file (min and max in metres, needed when the file carries no range); { location } cuts a survey at that latitude and longitude. Omitted, a landform preset is grounded on the real survey its kind names, and the result reports it as `ground` with its attribution.

heightmap.description: Path to a .png or .r16 height file, relative to the project.

min.description: Lowest elevation in the file, metres.

max.description: Highest elevation in the file, metres.

backdrop.description: "none" cooks no far ring. Omitted, an alpine or temperateMountains world on a survey gets ring.json: its survey continued to ten times the world's size, with one real whole mountain (a seeded pick, pose and height) standing past the playable square.

out.description: Relative directory under the project's assets.source that must not exist yet; the default is assets.source/worlds/<kit>.

name.description: The new biome's folder and look name; lowercase, no spaces.

overrides.description: IBiomeSpec fields to change on the base file (landform, foliage, grass, layers, water, spawn, species, aliases, bake). An unknown field fails. A species named `arbor:<preset>[@seed]` (for example arbor:oak@7) is a procedural Arbor tree the cook bakes and scatters; needs npm i -D @threenative/procedural-vegetation; set the row's far.impostor beyond 190 m, past the tree's last LOD. Presets: oak, beech, birch, spruce, scotspine, blackspruce, aspen, douglasfir, redcedar, bigleafmaple, cypress, olive, stonepine, acacia, baobab, coconut, banana, kapok, sakura, jmaple, ginkgo, bamboo, saguaro, joshua, fanpalm, araucaria, ipe, jacaranda.

ground.description: Where the ground comes from. "procedural" keeps the landform preset's own noise; { heightmap } names a 16-bit grayscale PNG or a square .r16 file (min and max in metres, needed when the file carries no range); { location } cuts a survey at that latitude and longitude. Omitted, a landform preset is grounded on the real survey its kind names, and the result reports it as `ground` with its attribution.

heightmap.description: Path to a .png or .r16 height file, relative to the project.

min.description: Lowest elevation in the file, metres.

descriptions.terrain_generate: Choose from a request, an explicit kit or a biome and cook one editable starter terrain kit (forest, coastal, alpine, desert or tundra) into a world.glb; `biome` names a starter or one of its alias words, or carries an inline IBiomeSpec whose own landform, size and seed build the ground; `landform` swaps the ground for one of the seven shape presets (alpine, temperateMountains, rollingHills, desertMesa, coastalCliffs, tundra, volcanic) and keeps the kit's surface and assets; `water` replaces the water bodies the biome declares and changes the cooked world: an ocean row floods to its level, a river or lake row re-shapes the recipe's own river or lake in order (width or radius), a recipe layer with no row is removed, and a river or lake row with no layer to take it fails. A `request`'s words also decide the landform (mountains, hills, mesa, cliffs, volcano), the water (river, lake, island, ocean), the features carved into any ground (canyon, gorge, ravine: a steep cut across it; fjord, inlet: a sea inlet into the land) and the size (huge, small: the biome's own size scaled); an explicit `landform`, `water` or `sizeMeters` wins over a word. A region word (european, boreal, mediterranean, pacific northwest) cooks that region's own world: the row's real survey as the ground, its plant community as the canopy (several species, each baked at more than one seed), and the starter's own surface, understorey and water, reported as `decided.region`. It keeps the starter's understorey, stones, road and water and replaces its canopy. A landform preset's ground is a real survey of the place its kind names, fetched from the AWS terrain tiles, resampled onto the recipe's grid, cooked with the attribution its source requires, and reported as `ground`; the preset's erosion and grain still run on top of it. `ground` replaces that choice: "procedural" cooks the preset's own noise, { heightmap } reads a 16-bit grayscale PNG or a square .r16 grid, { location } cuts a survey at a latitude and longitude. An alpine or temperateMountains world on a survey also writes ring.json, its survey continued to ten times the world's size with one real whole mountain from that range past the square, reported as `backdrop`; `backdrop: "none"` cooks none. The result's `decided` names each choice with the word behind it or `argument`, and `unused` lists the request words that named nothing. A request that names only a starter (no shape, water, feature, size, seed or ground of its own) is that starter as shipped, judged and measured, reported as `source: "catalog:<kit>"`; anything else is `"cooked"`. The reply's `seed` is the seed the world was cooked with: pass another `seed` for a variation of the same request. A request repeated in the same project is copied from its cook cache (`node_modules/.cache/threenative-terrain`) and reported as `cache: "hit"`. Returns the kit as recipe, the biome it bakes, the water bodies the cooked world floods, measured from the evaluated state as `water.json` records them, its band rows resolved against the cooked heights (`bands`), the world.glb, recipe.json and world.json paths, triangles, instances and draws measured from the produced GLB's default scene, a ctx.assets.model load snippet, and `grass`: the lines that grow the biome's grass rows as a streamed, swaying GrassField3D on the cooked ground through grassFieldFromBiome (null when the biome has no grass row; the blade and material come from the game's src/render/grass.ts). triangles counts every instance of the LOD0 default scene in full, before distance LOD and culling, instances sums the EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing instances, and draws counts primitives across instanced and non-instanced meshes, an instanced primitive counting once.
descriptions.terrain_biome_new: Make a new biome from a shipped one and cook it: copies the base biome's biome.data.json into <assets.source>/biomes/<name>/, applies the overrides, validates the file with validateBiome, then cooks it with the base kit's surface and assets and the biome's own landform preset. One call writes only under <assets.source>/biomes/<name>/, its cooked world included. Its ground comes from the biome's landform, the real survey that kind names unless `ground` names another source. Returns the same cook result as terrain_generate plus the biome file path and the biome's resolved `bands`. No code changes anywhere: the biome is data.
descriptions.terrain_patch: Apply editor commands (upsert, update, remove, move, toggle) to a terrain recipe and return the edited recipe.
